notes:
Overview: TidePool is evaluating Redwood Dedicated for low-latency baggage-routing assistant and real-time reranking in their carrier assignment pipeline. Primary ask: predictable throughput for peak windows (batch jobs + burst realtime), firm p99 latency commitments, and reserved GPU sizing guidance.

Key requirements: - Throughput: need sustained 10k token/s across 4 regions during peak nightly re-routes; daytime peaks ~2.5k token/s. - Latency SLOs: p50 < 40ms, p95 < 120ms, p99 < 250ms for chat/rerank endpoints. Tight for on-prem inference gateway + VPC. - Warm pools: want warm GPU pools to avoid cold-start KV-cache misses for heavy seq2seq runs. Prefer configurable warm pool size per model family. - Autoscaling: prefer predictive scale-up (pre-warm on schedule) + reactive scale-down with cooldown window; concerned about oscillation when traffic is spiky. - Queueing: must support bounded queue with backpressure and configurable max queue depth; SLA needs behavior defined when queue full (reject vs degrade). - Reserved planning: guidance on committed GPUs vs burst capacity; want runbook for forecast-driven reservation (monthly cadence) and rules for temporary burst billing. - Fallbacks: automatic routing to smaller quantized variants with graceful fallback and quality-tagging for downstream monitoring.

Recent timeline: - 2025-01-15: inbound from partner program, initial product intro (Aisha). - 2025-01-22: technical discovery call (Diego + infra team). Fireflies ff-2025-01-22-TP-01. Discussed current on-prem cluster (NVIDIA A100 x24) and desire to move critical inference into hybrid dedicated pools. - 2025-02-05: benchmark kick-off; TidePool provided sample workload + token distribution. - 2025-02-12: Redwood sent initial sizing: 12 reserved A100-equivalent GPUs per region (estimate). Slack notes: "Sizing looks conservative; can we drop to 8 if we pre-warm?" - 2025-02-14: scale policy deep-dive with infra leads. Fireflies ff-2025-02-14-TP-scale-review. Agreed to try predictive warm pool + PID-like cooldown to avoid thrash. - 2025-02-20: Received 24-hour baseline soak results (link in drive). p99 skewed during burst windows due to queueing.

Benchmark observations (from Redwood perf team): - Continuous batching gave 18% cost savings but increased p99 tail under sudden ramp when warm pool was empty. - Warm pool of ~30% of peak workers reduced cold-start p99 by ~60ms. - Reactive autoscale with 30s evaluation window caused frequent scale events; 3-min smoothing + predictive pre-warm recommended.

Open questions / risks: - SLA language: TidePool wants explicit credits for missed p99 in multi-region setups and a commitment for max cold-start time for new model variants. - Networking: VPC peering latency baseline required from infra; need trace for cross-region peering (asked by TidePool net team). - Cost sensitivity: CFO prefers smaller committed footprint; needs clear cost/benefit of reserved vs burst.

Next steps (short): - Diego to run 72h soak on a dedicated pool with 3 configs: baseline (no warm pool), warm-pool-30%, warm-pool-50% (action: 2025-02-24). - Redwood to provide SLA draft with explicit p99 definition and credit formula (action: Aisha, due 2025-02-28). - Schedule network latency baseline with TidePool net team (action: Lina). - Follow-up demo of autoscaler tuning knobs + live dashboard (demo booked week of 2025-03-03).

Quotes / paraphrases: - "We need predictability more than lowest cost — bursts are OK if billed, but p99 failures are not." — Head of ML infra. - "If warm pools solve the tail we can reduce reserved GPUs by ~25%" — infra lead.

Attachments / refs: drive soak report, perf deck, initial SLA draft (in linked drive). Jira: INF-4321 (scale flapping analysis), INF-4468 (network latency baseline).
